The '''1997 FA Cup final''' was the 116th final of the [[FA Cup]]. It took place on 17 May 1997 at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] and was contested by [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]], the [[North East England|North East]] club appearing in its first FA Cup Final.

Chelsea won 2–0 to win the FA Cup for the second time, the first having come in [[1970 FA Cup final|1970]]. It was also the club's first major trophy in 26 years.

It was the first major honour in the career of most Chelsea's players, but for [[Mark Hughes]], it was the fourth time that he had featured in an FA Cup winning side (having played on the winning [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] teams of [[1985 FA Cup final|1985]], [[1990 FA Cup final|1990]] and [[1994 FA Cup final|1994]]).<ref>{{cite web |title=Where are they now? Chelsea's 1997 FA Cup winners |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/where-are-they-now-chelseas-1997-fa-cup-winners |website=FourFourTwo |access-date=5 September 2020 |date=17 May 2017}}</ref> It was Middlesbrough's second defeat in a cup final in the [[1996–97 in English football|1996–97 season]] (they had also lost the [[1997 Football League Cup final|League Cup final]] to [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] the previous month), and they were also relegated from the Premier League.

==Match review==
Chelsea took the lead just 43 seconds into the match, with Italian midfielder [[Roberto Di Matteo]] receiving the ball and firing it into the goal off the crossbar from 25 [[yards]] to record what was at the time the quickest ever goal in a Wembley FA Cup final ([[Louis Saha]] broke this record 12 years later in the [[2009 FA Cup final|2009 final]] after just 25 seconds, coincidentally against Chelsea, though Chelsea won the match 2–1), breaking [[Jackie Milburn]]'s [[1955 FA Cup final|42-year record]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/ROBERTO'S+QUICKIE+MAKES+ROBBO+SICKIE!%3b+Blue+heaven+in+43+seconds.-a061133570
|title= ROBERTO'S QUICKIE MAKES ROBBO SICKIE!; Blue heaven in 43 seconds.|date=18 May 1997|work=The People (London)|access-date=21 November 2012 }}</ref>
Middlesbrough's prolific striker [[Fabrizio Ravanelli]] limped off after 21 minutes, further diminishing his side's chances of victory. Late in the first half [[Gianluca Festa]] put the ball in the net for Middlesbrough, but the goal was  controversially ruled out for offside. In a largely disappointing match, in which Chelsea were generally in control, Chelsea eventually added a second goal seven minutes from full-time with [[Eddie Newton (footballer)|Eddie Newton]] steering the ball into the net from [[Gianfranco Zola]]'s clever flick to seal a 2–0 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Blue+what+a+scorcher!%3b+CHELSEA+(1)+2%3b+Di+Matteo+1%2c+Newton+83+BORO+(0)...-a061141480
|title= Blue what a scorcher!
|date=18 May 1997|work=Sunday Mirror|access-date=21 November 2012 }}</ref>
